q.q: Which wall layer of the microsporangium mainly helps in the dehiscence of the anther?
q.e: The epidermis, endothecium and middle layers protect the microsporangium and help in dehiscence of the anther, the endothecium being the layer typically associated with the opening of the anther.

q.q: The androecium of a flower is made up of
q.e: The androecium is the male reproductive whorl and consists of stamens, each stamen having a filament and an anther; the gynoecium consists of pistils.

q.q: The sporogenous tissue of a microsporangium is located
o: in the centre of the microsporangium
between the endothecium and the middle layers
q.e: A compact homogeneous mass of sporogenous cells occupies the centre of each microsporangium, surrounded by the four wall layers.

q.q: Germ pores of a pollen grain are regions where
o: both intine and exine are absent
q.e: Germ pores are apertures in the pollen wall where sporopollenin, and therefore the exine, is absent; the intine remains continuous and the pollen tube emerges through these pores.

q.q: Which of the following is one of the most resistant organic materials known and forms the exine of the pollen grain?
q.e: Sporopollenin can withstand high temperature and strong acids and alkalis, and no enzyme that degrades it is known, which is why pollen exines are preserved as fossils.

q.q: In a pollen grain shed at the two-celled stage, the generative cell is
o: the cell with abundant food reserve
the cell with a large irregular nucleus
small, spindle-shaped and floating in the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell
q.e: The vegetative cell is the bigger one with abundant food reserve and a large irregularly shaped nucleus, while the generative cell is small and spindle-shaped and floats in the vegetative cell’s cytoplasm.

q.q: Papaver shows which condition of the gynoecium?
q.e: In Papaver the several pistils of the multicarpellary gynoecium are fused together, which is the syncarpous condition; free pistils, as in Michelia, make the gynoecium apocarpous.

q.q: The small opening in the integuments of the ovule through which the pollen tube usually enters is the
q.e: The integuments encircle the nucellus except at the tip, where a small opening called the micropyle is left; the pollen tube enters the ovule through it.

q.q: The megaspore mother cell can be identified in the nucellus by its
o: large size, dense cytoplasm and prominent nucleus
small size and highly vacuolated cytoplasm
position at the chalazal end outside the integuments
q.e: The MMC is a large cell with dense cytoplasm and a prominent nucleus; it is diploid and lies in the micropylar region of the nucellus, where it undergoes meiosis.

q.q: The number of nuclei present in the embryo sac just before cellularisation is
q.e: Successive free-nuclear mitotic divisions of the functional megaspore give the 2-nucleate, 4-nucleate and then the 8-nucleate embryo sac, after which cell walls are laid down.

q.q: Antipodal cells of the embryo sac are situated at the
o: lateral side of the central cell
q.e: Three cells are grouped together at the chalazal end and are called the antipodal cells; the three cells at the micropylar end form the egg apparatus.

q.q: Which structure guides the pollen tube into the synergid?
q.e: The synergids have special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip known as the filiform apparatus, which plays an important role in guiding the pollen tube into the synergid.

q.q: Pollination in Vallisneria is brought about by
o: long, ribbon-like pollen grains released under water
female flowers reaching the water surface on a long stalk while pollen drifts on the surface
wind carrying light pollen to large feathery stigmas
moths that lay their eggs inside the ovary
q.e: In Vallisneria the female flower is carried to the surface by a long stalk; the male flowers or pollen grains are released on to the water surface and are passively carried by the currents to the female flowers.

q.q: Pollen or nectar robbers are floral visitors that
o: pollinate the flower while feeding on it
lay their eggs inside the ovary locule
are essential for successful seed set
consume nectar or pollen without bringing about pollination
q.e: Such visitors take the floral reward but do not contact the anther and stigma in a way that transfers pollen, so no pollination results.

q.q: Monoecy, as seen in maize and castor, prevents
q.e: Unisexual flowers make autogamy impossible, but since both male and female flowers occur on the same plant, pollen can still travel from one flower to another of the same plant — geitonogamy. Only dioecy (papaya) prevents both.

q.q: All the events from the deposition of pollen on the stigma up to the entry of the pollen tube into the ovule are collectively called
q.e: Pollen-pistil interaction covers recognition of the pollen by the pistil, germination of compatible pollen, growth of the pollen tube through the style and its entry into the ovule.

q.q: Bagging of a flower in a plant breeding programme is done to
o: prevent contamination of the stigma with unwanted pollen
supply nutrients to the developing fruit
stop the anthers from dehiscing prematurely
accelerate the growth of the pollen tube
q.e: The emasculated flower is covered with a butter-paper bag so that only the pollen chosen by the breeder reaches the stigma, ensuring the purity of the cross.

q.q: In a species whose pollen is shed at the 3-celled stage, the pollen tube that enters the synergid carries
o: a vegetative cell and an undivided generative cell
a generative cell that divides inside the ovule
q.e: In 3-celled pollen the generative cell has already divided before shedding, so the pollen tube transports the two male gametes right from the beginning of its growth.

q.q: The primary endosperm nucleus of an angiosperm is
q.e: It is formed by the fusion of one haploid male gamete with the two haploid polar nuclei, so it is triploid (3n).

q.q: In a grass embryo, the sheath that encloses the radicle and the root cap is the
q.e: The coleorrhiza is the undifferentiated sheath covering the radicle and root cap, whereas the coleoptile is the hollow sheath enclosing the shoot apex and leaf primordia.

q.q: Which sequence correctly represents the development of a dicot embryo?
o: Zygote → pro-embryo → globular → heart-shaped → mature embryo
Zygote → globular → pro-embryo → heart-shaped → mature embryo
Pro-embryo → zygote → heart-shaped → globular → mature embryo
Zygote → heart-shaped → globular → pro-embryo → mature embryo
q.e: The zygote first forms a pro-embryo, which passes through the globular and then the heart-shaped stage before becoming the mature embryo.

q.q: Seedless bananas are produced as a result of
q.e: In parthenocarpy the ovary develops into a fruit without fertilisation, so no ovules mature into seeds. It can also be induced artificially with growth hormones.

q.q: Seeds of which of the following, about 2,000 years old and recovered from an archaeological excavation, were successfully germinated?
q.e: A date palm (Phoenix dactylifera) seed roughly 2,000 years old germinated successfully; Lupinus arcticus seeds from arctic tundra germinated after an estimated 10,000 years.

q.q: The additional embryos formed from nucellar cells in a Citrus seed are
o: genetically identical to the mother plant
q.e: Nucellar cells are somatic cells of the mother plant, so embryos arising from them by division are clonal — genetically identical to the parent — unlike the zygotic embryo in the same seed.

q.q: How many of the following are correctly paired — (1) Filament : stalk of the stamen, (2) Connective : joins the two thecae, (3) Theca : contains one microsporangium, (4) Thalamus : point of stamen attachment?
q.e: Filament, connective and thalamus are correctly described. Statement (3) is wrong: each theca contains two microsporangia, not one, giving four per anther in total.

q.q: A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed, with each lobe carrying how many microsporangia?
q.e: Each lobe (theca) of a bilobed anther carries two microsporangia at its corners, running longitudinally, giving four microsporangia in the whole anther.

q.q: A pollen grain measures roughly how many micrometres in diameter?
q.e: A pollen grain is generally spherical and measures about 25-50 micrometres in diameter, small enough to be invisible to the naked eye but visible under a microscope.

q.q: How many of the following statements about pollen grains are CORRECT — (1) about 60% of angiosperms shed pollen at the 3-celled stage, (2) the vegetative cell has a large irregular nucleus, (3) rice pollen loses viability within about 30 minutes, (4) pollen banks store grains at −196°C in liquid nitrogen?
q.e: All four statements are correct facts about pollen biology covered in this chapter: the 3-celled shedding stage, vegetative cell nucleus, short viability in rice, and cryostorage in pollen banks.

q.q: How many protective integuments typically cover an angiosperm ovule?
q.e: The ovule is covered by one or two protective integuments, which enclose it except at a small opening at the tip, the micropyle.

q.q: How many of the following statements about the ovary and ovules are CORRECT — (1) the ovary contains the ovarian cavity or locule, (2) the placenta bears the ovules inside the locule, (3) an ovary always contains only one ovule, (4) wheat and mango typically have a single ovule per ovary?
q.e: Statements (1), (2) and (4) are correct. Statement (3) is wrong — the number of ovules ranges from one (wheat, paddy, mango) to a very large number (papaya, watermelon, orchids), it is not always one.

q.q: The mature embryo sac has how many total nuclei?
q.e: The mature embryo sac has 8 nuclei in all: 2 synergids + 1 egg + 3 antipodals (6 nuclei in 6 cells) plus 2 polar nuclei sharing 1 central cell, giving 7 cells but 8 nuclei.

q.q: How many of the following are TRUE of monosporic embryo sac development — (1) it develops from a single functional megaspore, (2) the other three megaspores degenerate, (3) three successive mitoses occur, (4) the process needs no meiosis at all?
q.e: Statements (1), (2) and (3) are true. Statement (4) is false: megasporogenesis begins with meiosis of the MMC to form the tetrad, before the mitotic divisions of the functional megaspore even start.

q.q: How many of the following pairs are correctly matched — (1) Autogamy : same flower, (2) Geitonogamy : different flower, same plant, (3) Xenogamy : genetically different plant, (4) Cleistogamy : cross-pollination only?
q.e: (1), (2) and (3) are correct. (4) is wrong: cleistogamous flowers never open, so anther and stigma lie together and only autogamy (not cross-pollination) is possible.

q.q: Floral rewards offered to a pollinating animal typically include nectar and
q.e: Nectar and pollen grains are the two chief floral rewards offered to a pollinator; in some plants the reward instead is a safe place to lay eggs, as in Amorphophallus.

q.q: How many of the following are steps in artificial hybridisation when the female parent is bisexual — (1) emasculation, (2) bagging, (3) dusting the desired pollen, (4) re-bagging?
q.e: All four are the standard steps when the female parent is bisexual: emasculation, bagging, pollination with the desired pollen, and re-bagging until the fruit develops.

q.q: Pollen-pistil recognition is fundamentally based on a dialogue between
o: chemical components of pollen and pistil
the colour of pollen and stigma
the size of pollen and the width of the style
the temperature of the anther and the ovary
q.e: Recognition of compatible or incompatible pollen depends on a chemical dialogue between components of the pollen and components of the pistil, not on colour, size or temperature.

q.q: How many nuclei are involved in triple fusion?
q.e: Triple fusion involves three nuclei: one male gamete and the two polar nuclei of the central cell, together forming the triploid primary endosperm nucleus.

q.q: How many of the following statements about post-fertilisation development are CORRECT — (1) the endosperm develops before the embryo, (2) the zygote is retained inside the synergid, (3) the embryo develops at the micropylar end, (4) early embryo stages are similar in monocots and dicots?
q.e: Statements (1), (3) and (4) are correct. Statement (2) is wrong — the zygote lies within the embryo sac itself, not inside the synergid, which has already degenerated after discharging the male gametes.

q.q: How many of the following seeds are albuminous — wheat, castor, pea, coconut?
q.e: Wheat, castor and coconut retain their endosperm at maturity and are albuminous; pea is non-albuminous because its endosperm is fully consumed by the developing embryo.

q.q: The tough, protective seed coat of a mature seed develops from the
q.e: As the ovule matures into a seed, its integuments harden to form the tough, protective seed coat; the pericarp, by contrast, develops from the ovary wall to form the fruit wall.

q.q: The wall layer of the microsporangium that supplies nutrition to the developing pollen grains is the
q.e: The tapetum is the innermost wall layer of the microsporangium; its densely cytoplasmic, often multinucleate cells nourish the developing pollen grains.

q.q: A stamen consists of a filament and a terminal
q.e: A stamen has two parts: a filament and a terminal anther; the anther is the site of pollen production, while stigma, style and ovary belong to the pistil, not the stamen.

q.q: In a typical dithecous anther, the total number of microsporangia present is
q.e: A dithecous anther has two thecae, and each theca carries two microsporangia at its corners, giving four microsporangia in total.

q.q: How many of the following are TRUE of the androecium — (1) it is the male reproductive whorl, (2) it is made up of stamens, (3) each stamen has a filament and an anther, (4) it produces the egg cell?
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the androecium produces pollen, not the egg cell, which is produced in the gynoecium.

q.q: Tapetal cells are typically
o: binucleate or multinucleate with dense cytoplasm
q.e: Tapetal cells are highly specialised, with dense cytoplasm and usually more than one nucleus, a sign of their intense nutritive activity.

q.q: The inner layer of the pollen wall, made of cellulose and pectin, is the
q.e: The intine is the thin, continuous inner layer of the pollen wall, composed of cellulose and pectin, unlike the hard, sporopollenin-based exine.

q.q: In pollen grains shed at the 2-celled stage, the larger cell with abundant food reserve is the
q.e: The vegetative cell is larger, with abundant food reserve and a large irregularly shaped nucleus; the generative cell is small and spindle-shaped, floating in the vegetative cell's cytoplasm.

q.q: Pollen of carrot grass (Parthenium) is notorious for causing
q.e: Pollen of Parthenium (carrot grass) causes allergies and respiratory disorders such as asthma and bronchitis in sensitive people.

q.q: Pollen viability in rice and wheat is typically lost within about
q.e: Pollen viability depends on temperature and humidity. In rice and wheat, pollen loses viability within about 30 minutes of release, unlike Rosaceae, Leguminosae and Solanaceae, where it lasts for months.

q.q: How many of the following statements about pollen storage and viability are CORRECT — (1) pollen can be stored for years in liquid nitrogen at about −196°C, (2) all pollen loses viability within 30 minutes regardless of species, (3) pollen banks are comparable to seed or gene banks, (4) viability depends only on genetics, never on temperature or humidity?
q.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong — only rice/wheat-type pollen loses viability that fast, while Rosaceae, Leguminosae and Solanaceae pollen lasts months. Statement 4 is wrong — viability depends on temperature and humidity.

q.q: The basal part of an ovule, lying opposite the micropylar end, is the
q.e: The chalaza is the basal part of the ovule, lying opposite the micropylar end.

q.q: The number of ovules found in the ovary of papaya or watermelon is best described as
q.e: The number of ovules in an ovary may be one, as in wheat, paddy and mango, to many, as in papaya, watermelon and orchids.

q.q: A flower whose gynoecium is made up of a single pistil is termed
q.e: A flower with a single pistil is monocarpellary; with more than one pistil it is multicarpellary, which may be syncarpous (fused) or apocarpous (free).

q.q: The megaspore mother cell undergoes meiosis to ultimately form a tetrad of how many haploid megaspores?
q.e: The megaspore mother cell undergoes meiosis, passing through a dyad stage, to form a megaspore tetrad of four haploid megaspores.

q.q: How many of the following statements about the ovule are CORRECT — (1) the funicle attaches the ovule to the placenta, (2) the hilum is the junction of the funicle and the ovule body, (3) the nucellus lies outside the integuments, (4) the micropyle is the opening left uncovered by the integuments?
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the nucellus lies within (enclosed by) the integuments, not outside them.

q.q: The three cells grouped at the micropylar end of a mature embryo sac, apart from the egg cell, are the
q.e: The egg apparatus at the micropylar end consists of two synergids and one egg cell; the two synergids together with the egg cell make up this group of three.

q.q: Cellularisation of the free-nuclear embryo sac occurs after the
q.e: After the free-nuclear divisions produce a 2-, then 4-, then 8-nucleate embryo sac, cellularisation follows, laying down cell walls around six of the eight nuclei.

q.q: The special thickenings at the micropylar tip of the synergids are collectively called the
q.e: The synergids bear special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called the filiform apparatus, which plays a key role in guiding the pollen tube into the synergid.

q.q: The mature embryo sac of a typical angiosperm is described as 7-celled but how many-nucleate?
q.e: Six of the eight nuclei organise into cells (2 synergids + 1 egg + 3 antipodals), while the remaining two, the polar nuclei, share one central cell, giving 7 cells but 8 nuclei.

q.q: How many of the following are TRUE of the antipodal cells — (1) there are three of them, (2) they lie at the chalazal end, (3) they are part of the egg apparatus, (4) they may degenerate after fertilisation along with the synergids?
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the egg apparatus (two synergids and one egg cell) lies at the micropylar end, while the antipodals are a separate group at the chalazal end.

q.q: Which of the following is an abiotic agent of pollination?
q.e: Pollination depends on external agents that are either abiotic (wind, water) or biotic (animals such as bees, birds and bats); wind is the most common abiotic mode.

q.q: Continued self-pollination over generations chiefly leads to
q.e: Continued self-pollination causes inbreeding depression, so many plants have evolved outbreeding devices to discourage autogamy and encourage cross-pollination.

q.q: The reward offered by Amorphophallus, the tallest flower, to its pollinator is
o: a safe place to lay eggs
q.e: Floral rewards offered to pollinators are typically nectar and pollen grains; in some plants the reward is a safe place to lay eggs, as in Amorphophallus, the tallest flower.

q.q: How many kinds of flowers, chasmogamous and cleistogamous, are typically borne on plants such as Viola and Oxalis?
q.e: Plants such as Viola, Oxalis and Commelina bear two kinds of flowers: chasmogamous flowers that open normally and cleistogamous flowers that never open.

q.q: How many of the following outbreeding devices are correctly described — (1) non-synchrony of pollen release and stigma receptivity, (2) anther and stigma placed at different positions, (3) self-incompatibility blocking pollen-tube growth, (4) production of bisexual flowers only?
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the actual outbreeding device is the production of unisexual flowers (monoecy or dioecy), not bisexual flowers.

q.q: The genetic mechanism that inhibits germination of self-pollen or the growth of its pollen tube in the pistil is called
q.e: Self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen from germinating or inhibits growth of the pollen tube in the pistil, acting as an outbreeding device.

q.q: The full path of a compatible pollen tube after germination is stigma → style → ovary → micropyle →
q.e: Guided by the filiform apparatus, the pollen tube's full route is stigma → style → ovary → micropyle → filiform apparatus → synergid, one of the two synergids of the egg apparatus.

q.q: When the female parent in a hybridisation programme bears unisexual flowers, the step that can be skipped is
q.e: When the female parent bears unisexual flowers, there are no anthers to remove, so emasculation is not necessary; bagging, pollination and re-bagging are still carried out.

q.q: How many key steps make up artificial hybridisation on a bisexual flower — emasculation, bagging, pollination, re-bagging?
q.e: When the female parent is bisexual, artificial hybridisation has four key steps: emasculation, bagging, pollination (dusting the desired pollen), and re-bagging.

q.q: How many of the following statements about pollen-pistil interaction are CORRECT — (1) it depends on chemical recognition, (2) incompatible pollen is always accepted, (3) the pistil can inhibit pollen-tube growth, (4) it ends the moment pollen lands on the stigma?
q.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong — incompatible pollen is rejected, not accepted. Statement 4 is wrong — the interaction continues up to entry of the pollen tube into the ovule, not just deposition.

q.q: Syngamy in an angiosperm results in the formation of the
q.e: In syngamy, one male gamete fuses with the egg cell, and their nuclei fuse to form the diploid (2n) zygote; triple fusion, a separate event, forms the primary endosperm nucleus.

q.q: The white kernel of a coconut represents the
q.e: After the free-nuclear stage (represented by coconut water), cell walls are laid down, making the endosperm cellular; the white kernel of the coconut is this cellular endosperm.

q.q: In a dicot embryo, the epicotyl ends in the
q.e: The epicotyl is the portion of the embryonal axis above the level of attachment of the cotyledons; it ends in the plumule (shoot tip), while the hypocotyl below ends in the radicle.

q.q: How many cotyledons does a typical dicot embryo possess?
q.e: A dicot embryo consists of an embryonal axis and two cotyledons, often fleshy with stored food, distinguishing it from the single cotyledon (scutellum) of a monocot embryo.

q.q: How many of the following are CORRECT about double fertilisation — (1) it is unique to flowering plants, (2) syngamy forms the zygote, (3) triple fusion involves three nuclei, (4) both male gametes fuse with the egg cell?
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: only one male gamete fuses with the egg cell (syngamy); the other fuses with the two polar nuclei (triple fusion), not with the egg cell.

q.q: Seeds whose reserve food is completely consumed by the embryo during development, such as pea and groundnut, are called
q.e: Non-albuminous (ex-albuminous) seeds, such as pea, groundnut and beans, have their endosperm completely consumed during embryo development, unlike albuminous seeds where it persists.

q.q: The persistent, residual nucellus seen in seeds such as black pepper and beet is called
q.e: Perisperm is the residual, persistent nucellus seen in some seeds such as black pepper and beet, distinct from the endosperm, which arises after fertilisation.

q.q: Nucellar polyembryony, where additional embryos arise from nucellar tissue, is commonly seen in
q.e: Nucellar polyembryony is seen in Citrus and mango: some nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac divide, protrude into it, and develop into additional embryos genetically identical to the mother plant.

q.q: A Phoenix dactylifera (date palm) seed recovered from an archaeological excavation and successfully germinated was about how many years old?
q.e: A Phoenix dactylifera (date palm) seed about 2,000 years old was successfully germinated, illustrating the remarkably long periods for which seeds can retain viability.

q.q: How many of the following are CORRECT about seed structure — (1) the seed coat develops from the integuments, (2) the micropyle persists as a pore for water and oxygen entry, (3) cotyledons are always devoid of reserve food, (4) the embryonal axis is part of the seed?
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: cotyledons are often thick and swollen with reserve food, not devoid of it.

q.q: Each testicular lobule of a human testis contains
q.e: Each testis has about 250 compartments called testicular lobules, and each lobule contains one to three highly coiled seminiferous tubules in which sperms are produced.

q.q: Which of the following is the single (unpaired) accessory gland in the human male reproductive system?
q.e: The male accessory glands are a pair of seminal vesicles, a pair of bulbourethral (Cowper’s) glands and a single prostate gland.

q.q: Seminal plasma contributes approximately what percentage of the volume of semen?
q.e: The secretions of the seminal vesicles, prostate and bulbourethral glands together form the seminal plasma, which makes up roughly 60% of the semen volume; the sperms form the rest.

q.q: The part of the oviduct that lies between the infundibulum and the isthmus is the
q.e: The infundibulum leads to a wider part called the ampulla, which is followed by the narrow isthmus that joins the uterus. The ampullary–isthmic junction is the usual site of fertilisation.

q.q: The thick middle layer of the uterine wall made of smooth muscle, which shows strong contractions during delivery, is the
q.e: The uterine wall has three layers — perimetrium (external), myometrium (middle smooth muscle) and endometrium (inner lining). The myometrium generates the strong contractions of labour.

q.q: The milk-secreting alveoli of the mammary gland are best described as
q.e: Each breast has 15–20 mammary lobes containing clusters of cells called alveoli. These alveoli are modified sweat glands that secrete milk, which is stored in their cavities.

q.q: The release of sperms from the Sertoli cells into the lumen of the seminiferous tubule is called
q.e: After spermiogenesis, the sperm heads remain embedded in the Sertoli cells and are finally released into the lumen of the seminiferous tubule; this release is called spermiation.

q.q: In the human male, LH is also known as ICSH because it acts on
o: the interstitial cells of the testis
q.e: LH is called Interstitial Cell Stimulating Hormone (ICSH) in males because it acts on the Leydig cells, i.e. the interstitial cells, stimulating them to secrete androgens such as testosterone.

q.q: How many primary follicles are left in each ovary of a human female at the time of puberty?
q.e: Millions of oogonia are formed in the foetal ovary, but a large number of primary follicles degenerate before puberty, so only 60,000–80,000 primary follicles are left in each ovary at puberty.

q.q: The menstrual phase of the human menstrual cycle normally lasts for:
q.e: The menstrual flow (menses) lasts about 3–5 days and consists of blood, mucus and cellular debris of the endometrium.

q.q: Progesterone essential for the maintenance of the endometrium during the luteal phase is secreted by the:
q.e: The remains of the ruptured Graafian follicle transform into the corpus luteum, which secretes large amounts of progesterone to maintain the endometrium for a possible pregnancy.

q.q: In a normal 28-day menstrual cycle, on which day do LH and FSH attain their peak levels?
q.e: LH and FSH peak in the middle of the cycle, around day 14. The LH surge at this point induces rupture of the Graafian follicle and ovulation.

q.q: Completion of meiosis-II in the secondary oocyte is induced by:
o: Entry of the sperm into the ovum
Secretion of progesterone by the corpus luteum
q.e: Entry of the sperm stimulates the secondary oocyte to complete meiosis-II, producing a haploid ovum (ootid) and a second polar body; the two haploid nuclei then fuse to form the diploid zygote.

q.q: Cleavage of the human zygote begins as it moves through the:
q.e: The mitotic cleavage divisions start while the zygote moves through the isthmus of the fallopian tube towards the uterus, forming 2, 4, 8, 16 blastomeres.

q.q: Which statement about human sex determination is correct?
o: All sperms carry a Y chromosome
The ova are of two types, X-bearing and Y-bearing
The sex of the baby is determined by the father
Sex is decided at the time of implantation
q.e: The human female is XX and produces only X-bearing ova; the male is XY and produces 50% X and 50% Y sperms. Since sex is decided at fertilisation by the type of sperm, the father determines the sex of the baby.

q.q: The milk produced during the initial days of lactation, rich in antibodies, is called:
q.e: Colostrum is the first milk secreted after childbirth. It contains several antibodies that are essential for developing resistance (immunity) in the new-born baby.

q.q: Parturition is best described as an example of:
o: A positive feedback neuroendocrine mechanism involving oxytocin
A negative feedback mechanism involving prolactin
A purely nervous reflex with no hormonal component
A purely hormonal event controlled only by the placenta
q.e: The foetal ejection reflex triggers oxytocin release, oxytocin causes stronger uterine contractions, and these stimulate still more oxytocin — a classic positive feedback neuroendocrine loop ending in expulsion of the foetus.

q.q: Which set of hormones is secreted in the human female only during pregnancy?
q.e: hCG, hPL and relaxin are produced only during pregnancy. The other hormones listed are also secreted in the non-pregnant state, though their levels rise several-fold during pregnancy.

q.q: The male copulatory organ, composed of spongy erectile tissue, is the
q.e: The penis is the male external genital organ and copulatory organ, made of spongy erectile tissue (corpora cavernosa and corpus spongiosum).

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the male reproductive system are CORRECT?
1. The prostate is a single gland.
2. Leydig cells lie inside the seminiferous tubules.
3. Sertoli cells nourish the developing germ cells.
4. The scrotum keeps the testes warmer than body temperature.
q.e: Correct statements: 1 (prostate is single) and 3 (Sertoli cells nourish germ cells). Statement 2 is wrong — Leydig cells lie OUTSIDE the tubules in the interstitial spaces. Statement 4 is wrong — the scrotum keeps testes COOLER, not warmer.

q.q: If the normal scrotal temperature is about 35°C and normal core body temperature is about 37.5°C, this roughly reflects a temperature difference of
q.e: The scrotum maintains the testes roughly 2–2.5°C cooler than core body temperature, which matches a drop from about 37.5°C to about 35°C.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the female reproductive system are CORRECT?
1. The ovary is covered by a thin epithelium.
2. The infundibulum bears fimbriae that collect the ovum.
3. The myometrium is the innermost uterine layer.
4. The mammary alveoli are modified sweat glands.
q.e: Correct: 1, 2 and 4. Statement 3 is wrong — the myometrium is the MIDDLE muscular layer; the endometrium is the innermost layer.

q.q: If a woman's oviduct is 11 cm long and the ampulla makes up about 55% of that length, approximately how long is the ampulla?
q.e: 55% of 11 cm = 0.55 × 11 = 6.05 cm, illustrating that the ampulla is the longest single segment of the 10–12 cm oviduct.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about gametogenesis are CORRECT?
1. Spermatogenesis begins at puberty.
2. Oogenesis begins during foetal life.
3. One primary oocyte yields four functional ova.
4. A primary spermatocyte is diploid.
q.e: Correct: 1, 2 and 4. Statement 3 is wrong — one primary oocyte yields only ONE functional ovum, the rest becoming polar bodies.

q.q: If 60 primary spermatocytes complete spermatogenesis normally, the number of functional sperms produced is
q.e: Each primary spermatocyte yields 4 sperms (via 2 secondary spermatocytes, each giving 2 spermatids). So 60 × 4 = 240 sperms.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the menstrual cycle are CORRECT?
1. Menarche marks the first menstruation.
2. The menstrual cycle is found in all mammals.
3. The LH surge occurs at the middle of the cycle.
4. Progesterone is secreted mainly by the corpus luteum.
q.e: Correct: 1, 3 and 4. Statement 2 is wrong — the menstrual cycle is found only in primates; other mammals show the oestrous cycle.

q.q: If menarche occurs at 13 years and menopause at 50 years, for approximately how many years does a woman experience menstrual cycles?
q.e: 50 − 13 = 37 years, the approximate span of the reproductive (menstruating) phase between menarche and menopause.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about fertilisation are CORRECT?
1. Fertilisation occurs at the ampullary-isthmic junction.
2. The zona pellucida blocks polyspermy.
3. The zygote is haploid.
4. Sex is decided at the moment of fertilisation.
q.e: Correct: 1, 2 and 4. Statement 3 is wrong — the zygote formed by fusion of two haploid nuclei is DIPLOID, not haploid.

q.q: In a batch of 500 sperms reaching the vicinity of an ovum, if only sperms carrying an X chromosome are counted, approximately how many would that be?
q.e: Since 50% of sperms carry X and 50% carry Y, about half of 500, i.e. 250, would be X-bearing.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about pregnancy and parturition are CORRECT?
1. The placenta secretes hCG.
2. Oxytocin causes milk secretion.
3. Gastrulation forms three germ layers.
4. The gestation period is about 9 months.
q.e: Correct: 1, 3 and 4. Statement 2 is wrong — oxytocin causes milk EJECTION, not secretion; prolactin controls milk secretion.

q.q: If a baby is born exactly 40 weeks after fertilisation, and the first trimester ends at 12 weeks, approximately what fraction of the full gestation does the first trimester represent?
q.e: 12 weeks out of 40 weeks is 30%, i.e. less than one-third of the full gestation period.

q.q: Sperms are transported and stored by the
q.e: The accessory ducts (rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis, vas deferens) store and transport sperms from the testis to the outside.

q.q: Which sequence correctly represents the pathway followed by sperms after release from the seminiferous tubule?
o: Rete testis → vasa efferentia → epididymis → vas deferens
Rete testis → epididymis → vasa efferentia → vas deferens
Vasa efferentia → rete testis → epididymis → vas deferens
Epididymis → rete testis → vasa efferentia → vas deferens
q.e: The correct pathway is: rete testis → vasa efferentia → epididymis → vas deferens → ejaculatory duct → urethra.

q.q: The narrow part of the oviduct that joins the uterus is the
q.e: The isthmus is the narrow terminal part of the oviduct that joins the uterus.

q.q: Which of the following statements regarding the female reproductive system is INCORRECT?
o: The uterus opens into the vagina via the cervix
The labia minora lie beneath the labia majora
The perimetrium is the innermost uterine layer
Mammary glands are accessory reproductive structures
q.e: The perimetrium is the OUTERMOST (not innermost) uterine layer; the endometrium is the innermost. The other statements are correct.

q.q: The enzyme-filled cap over the anterior part of the sperm head is the
q.e: The acrosome is the enzyme-filled cap over the anterior part of the sperm head that helps penetrate the ovum's coverings.

q.q: Which of the following statements about oogenesis is INCORRECT?
o: The antrum appears at the secondary follicle stage
Oogonia are formed only during foetal life
A primary follicle has a primary oocyte surrounded by granulosa cells
Meiosis-I is completed at the tertiary follicle stage
q.e: The antrum (fluid-filled cavity) appears at the TERTIARY follicle stage, not the secondary follicle stage. The other statements are correct.

q.q: The breakdown of the endometrial lining and its blood vessels results in the
q.e: Menstrual flow is the periodic discharge of blood, mucus and cellular debris resulting from breakdown of the endometrial lining and its blood vessels.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT a correct statement about the luteal phase?
o: If fertilisation occurs, the corpus luteum degenerates immediately
This phase precedes the next menstrual phase if fertilisation fails
q.e: If fertilisation OCCURS, the corpus luteum is MAINTAINED, not degenerated; it degenerates only when fertilisation fails to occur.

q.q: The mitotic divisions of the zygote that produce blastomeres are called
q.e: Cleavage is the series of mitotic divisions of the zygote that produces blastomeres (2, 4, 8, 16 cells).

q.q: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of early human development.
q.e: Development proceeds: zygote → cleavage forms the morula → morula transforms into the blastocyst → the blastocyst implants in the endometrium.

q.q: Which of the following statements about sex determination is INCORRECT?
o: An X-bearing sperm fertilising the ovum gives an XX zygote that develops into a female
The mother determines the sex of the child since she contributes the X chromosome
A Y-bearing sperm fertilising the ovum gives an XY zygote that develops into a male
All ova carry an X chromosome
q.e: It is the FATHER, not the mother, who determines the sex of the child, since it is the type of sperm (X or Y) — not the ovum, which always carries X — that decides the outcome.

q.q: Which structure supplies oxygen and nutrients to the developing foetus and removes carbon dioxide and waste?
q.e: The placenta facilitates the supply of oxygen and nutrients to the foetus and the removal of carbon dioxide and excretory materials.

q.q: Arrange the following stages of parturition in the correct sequence.
o: Oxytocin release → foetal ejection reflex → expulsion of baby → stronger contractions
Stronger contractions → foetal ejection reflex → oxytocin release → expulsion of baby
Expulsion of baby → foetal ejection reflex → oxytocin release → stronger contractions
Foetal ejection reflex → oxytocin release → stronger contractions → expulsion of baby
q.e: Parturition proceeds: foetal ejection reflex (mild contractions from foetal/placental signals) → oxytocin release from the posterior pituitary → stronger contractions (positive feedback) → expulsion of the baby.

q.q: Which of the following statements about placental hormones is INCORRECT?
o: Relaxin is produced early, before implantation, not later in pregnancy
hCG is detected in early pregnancy tests
hPL is produced by the placenta
Progestogens from the placenta help maintain pregnancy
q.e: Relaxin is produced in the LATER phase of pregnancy, not before implantation. The other statements about hCG, hPL and progestogens are correct.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about semen are CORRECT?
1. Seminal plasma is rich in fructose, calcium and enzymes.
2. Semen consists only of sperms with no other fluid.
3. Seminal plasma is alkaline.
4. Fructose provides energy to sperms.
q.e: Correct: 1, 3 and 4. Statement 2 is wrong — semen is sperms PLUS seminal plasma, not sperms alone.

q.q: If a testis has approximately 250 lobules and each lobule has an average of 2 seminiferous tubules, approximately how many seminiferous tubules does one testis have?
q.e: 250 lobules × 2 tubules per lobule = approximately 500 seminiferous tubules per testis.

q.q: Which of the following correctly lists structures found in the female external genitalia?
o: Corpus luteum, Graafian follicle, primary follicle
Mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, hymen, clitoris
q.e: The female external genitalia include the mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, hymen and clitoris. The other options list internal duct parts, uterine layers, or ovarian follicle stages.

q.q: If each breast has 18 mammary lobes on average, how many mammary lobes would a woman have in total across both breasts?
q.e: 18 lobes per breast × 2 breasts = 36 mammary lobes in total, consistent with the normal range of 15–20 lobes per breast.

q.q: Which of the following correctly matches a hormone with its action in the male?
o: GnRH — acts directly on the testis
q.e: FSH acts on Sertoli cells to help spermiogenesis; LH acts on Leydig cells to stimulate androgen secretion; GnRH acts on the anterior pituitary, not directly on the testis.

q.q: Arrange the following stages of oogenesis in the correct order.
o: Primary oocyte → oogonium → ovum → secondary oocyte
Secondary oocyte → primary oocyte → oogonium → ovum
Oogonium → primary oocyte → secondary oocyte → ovum
Ovum → secondary oocyte → primary oocyte → oogonium
q.e: Oogenesis proceeds: oogonium (mitotic multiplication) → primary oocyte (arrested at prophase-I) → secondary oocyte (after meiosis-I at the tertiary follicle stage) → ovum (after meiosis-II, completed upon sperm entry).

q.q: Which of the following correctly matches a menstrual cycle phase with its dominant event?
o: Menstrual phase — secretion of progesterone by the corpus luteum
Follicular phase — rupture of the Graafian follicle
Luteal phase — regeneration of the endometrium by oestrogen
Ovulatory phase — LH surge and release of the ovum
q.e: The ovulatory phase is marked by the LH surge and release of the ovum. Progesterone secretion belongs to the luteal phase, follicle rupture belongs to the ovulatory phase, and endometrial regeneration by oestrogen belongs to the follicular phase.

q.q: If a woman's menstrual phase lasts 4 days out of a 28-day cycle, approximately what percentage of the cycle does the menstrual phase represent?
q.e: 4/28 × 100 ≈ 14.3%, so the menstrual phase represents roughly 14% of a typical 28-day cycle.

q.q: Which of the following correctly matches a structure with its role in fertilisation and early development?
o: Zona pellucida — blocks entry of additional sperms
Inner cell mass — attaches to the endometrium
q.e: The zona pellucida blocks polyspermy after the first sperm's entry. The inner cell mass (not the trophoblast) forms the embryo, the ampullary-isthmic junction (not the isthmus alone) is the fertilisation site, and the trophoblast (not the inner cell mass) attaches to the endometrium.

q.q: Which of the following correctly matches a gestational milestone with its approximate timing?
o: First foetal movements — end of first month
Eyelids separating — end of first month
Heart formation — end of first month
q.e: The heart is formed by the end of the first month. First foetal movements occur in the fifth month, eyelids separate by 24 weeks, and limbs form by the end of the second month, not the ninth.

q.q: If a foetus's heart forms at week 4 and the first movements are felt at week 20, approximately how many weeks separate these two milestones?
q.e: 20 − 4 = 16 weeks separate the formation of the heart (end of first month) and the first foetal movements (around the fifth month).

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the male reproductive system are CORRECT?
1. The testes lie inside the scrotum, which keeps them about 2–2.5°C cooler than body temperature. 2. Each testis has about 250 lobules, and each lobule contains 1 to 3 seminiferous tubules. 3. Leydig cells lie inside the seminiferous tubules and nourish the germ cells. 4. The vas deferens is a paired accessory gland.
q.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — Leydig cells lie OUTSIDE the tubules in the interstitial spaces (Sertoli cells nourish germ cells). Statement 4 is wrong — the vas deferens is a duct, not a gland.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the male reproductive system are CORRECT?
1. Sertoli cells respond to FSH and nourish the developing germ cells. 2. LH is also called ICSH in the male and acts on Leydig cells. 3. Spermatogonia are haploid cells lying on the outer wall of the seminiferous tubule. 4. The epididymis is a straight, uncoiled tube.
q.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — spermatogonia are DIPLOID and lie on the INNER wall of the tubule. Statement 4 is wrong — the epididymis is highly coiled.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the male reproductive system are CORRECT?
1. The accessory ducts include the rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis and vas deferens. 2. The prostate is a single (unpaired) accessory gland. 3. Seminal vesicles are single, unpaired glands. 4. Bulbourethral glands lubricate the penis during coitus.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — seminal vesicles are PAIRED glands.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the male reproductive system are CORRECT?
1. The mitochondria in a sperm's middle piece generate ATP for tail movement. 2. The acrosome is located in the sperm's tail. 3. A sperm's entire body is enclosed by a plasma membrane. 4. Semen consists only of sperms, with no fluid component.
q.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong — the acrosome is in the HEAD. Statement 4 is wrong — semen also contains seminal plasma from the accessory glands.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the male reproductive system are CORRECT?
1. Interstitial spaces lie outside the seminiferous tubules and contain Leydig cells. 2. Androgens secreted by Leydig cells stimulate spermatogenesis. 3. FSH acts directly on spermatogonia to convert them into spermatozoa. 4. GnRH from the hypothalamus stimulates the anterior pituitary to release LH and FSH.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — FSH acts on Sertoli cells (not directly on spermatogonia) to aid spermiogenesis.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the male reproductive system are CORRECT?
1. Vasa efferentia carry sperms from the rete testis to the epididymis. 2. Sperms mature and gain motility partly due to secretions of the epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles and prostate. 3. The scrotum keeps testes warmer than the abdominal cavity. 4. Each seminiferous tubule contains only Sertoli cells and no germ cells.
q.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — the scrotum keeps testes COOLER. Statement 4 is wrong — the tubule wall has both germ cells and Sertoli cells.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the female reproductive system are CORRECT?
1. The infundibulum bears fimbriae that help collect the ovum after ovulation. 2. The isthmus is the widest part of the oviduct. 3. Each oviduct is about 10–12 cm long. 4. The uterus opens into the vagina through the isthmus.
q.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong — the ampulla, not the isthmus, is the widest part. Statement 4 is wrong — the uterus opens into the vagina through the cervix.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the female reproductive system are CORRECT?
1. The myometrium is the thick muscular middle layer of the uterus. 2. The endometrium undergoes cyclic changes during the menstrual cycle. 3. The perimetrium is the innermost uterine layer. 4. The cervix connects the uterus to the vagina.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — the endometrium (not perimetrium) is the innermost layer; the perimetrium is the thin outer membranous layer.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the female reproductive system are CORRECT?
1. The ovary is covered externally by a thick muscular layer. 2. Each human ovary is about 2–4 cm long. 3. The ovarian stroma has a peripheral cortex and inner medulla. 4. Ovaries are connected to the pelvic wall and uterus by ligaments.
q.e: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong — the ovary is covered by a thin epithelium, not a thick muscular layer.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the female reproductive system are CORRECT?
1. The mons pubis is a cushion of fatty tissue covered by skin and pubic hair. 2. The labia majora lie beneath the labia minora. 3. The clitoris is a tiny erectile structure at the junction of the labia minora. 4. The hymen reliably confirms a woman's virginity in every case.
q.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong — the labia majora lie OUTSIDE, with the labia minora beneath them. Statement 4 is wrong — the hymen is not a reliable indicator of virginity.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the female reproductive system are CORRECT?
1. Each breast contains 15–20 mammary lobes made of alveoli. 2. Alveoli of the mammary gland are modified sweat glands. 3. Milk moves from alveoli directly to the nipple with no intermediate ducts. 4. A functional mammary gland becomes fully active only after childbirth.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — milk passes through mammary tubules, ducts, the ampulla and the lactiferous duct before reaching the nipple.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the female reproductive system are CORRECT?
1. Milk secretion is controlled by prolactin from the anterior pituitary. 2. Milk ejection is controlled by oxytocin from the posterior pituitary. 3. The vagina is the site of fertilisation. 4. The female external genitalia include the mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, hymen and clitoris.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — fertilisation occurs at the ampullary-isthmic junction of the oviduct, not the vagina.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about gametogenesis are CORRECT?
1. Gametogenesis is the formation of gametes by meiosis from a diploid mother cell. 2. Spermatogenesis begins only at puberty. 3. Oogenesis also begins only at puberty, like spermatogenesis. 4. One primary spermatocyte gives rise to four haploid spermatids.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — oogenesis begins during embryonic (foetal) life, unlike spermatogenesis.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about gametogenesis are CORRECT?
1. A primary oocyte surrounded by granulosa cells is called a primary follicle. 2. A secondary follicle becomes a tertiary follicle upon developing a fluid-filled antrum. 3. The Graafian follicle is the stage before the primary follicle. 4. Ovulation is the rupture of the Graafian follicle, releasing the ovum.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — the Graafian follicle is the LAST stage, formed after the primary, secondary and tertiary follicle stages, just before ovulation.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about gametogenesis are CORRECT?
1. GnRH is secreted by the hypothalamus. 2. FSH acts on Sertoli cells to aid spermiogenesis. 3. LH acts on Sertoli cells to stimulate androgen secretion. 4. Androgens secreted by Leydig cells stimulate spermatogenesis.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — LH acts on Leydig cells (not Sertoli cells) to stimulate androgen secretion.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about gametogenesis are CORRECT?
1. The acrosome contains enzymes that help the sperm penetrate the ovum's coverings. 2. The sperm's middle piece is packed with mitochondria. 3. The sperm tail's lashing movements give it motility. 4. The sperm head contains no nucleus.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong — the sperm head contains an elongated haploid nucleus.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about gametogenesis are CORRECT?
1. Oogonia are formed throughout a woman's adult reproductive life. 2. Primary oocytes are arrested at prophase-I until puberty. 3. At puberty, 60,000–80,000 primary follicles remain in each ovary. 4. The first meiotic division of the primary oocyte is equal, producing two identical cells.
q.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong — oogonia are formed only during foetal life. Statement 4 is wrong — the first meiotic division is unequal.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about gametogenesis are CORRECT?
1. One primary oocyte ultimately produces one functional ovum plus polar bodies. 2. Spermiation is the release of mature sperm heads (still embedded in Sertoli cells) into the tubule lumen. 3. A secondary spermatocyte is diploid. 4. Meiosis-II of the secondary spermatocyte produces spermatids.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — a secondary spermatocyte is HAPLOID, formed after meiosis-I.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the menstrual cycle are CORRECT?
1. The menstrual cycle repeats about every 28–29 days in human females. 2. Menarche typically occurs at 12–15 years of age. 3. Menopause occurs around 25 years of age. 4. One ovum is normally released around the middle of each cycle.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — menopause occurs around 50 years of age, not 25.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the menstrual cycle are CORRECT?
1. The follicular phase is also called the proliferative phase. 2. The luteal phase is also called the secretory phase. 3. Ovulation occurs during the menstrual phase. 4. FSH and LH peak at mid-cycle, triggering ovulation.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — ovulation occurs during the ovulatory phase around day 14, not the menstrual phase.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the menstrual cycle are CORRECT?
1. The corpus luteum secretes progesterone. 2. If fertilisation occurs, the corpus luteum degenerates immediately. 3. Menstrual flow includes blood, mucus and endometrial debris. 4. Absence of menstruation is always due to disease, never pregnancy.
q.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong — if fertilisation occurs, the corpus luteum is MAINTAINED. Statement 4 is wrong — absence of menstruation is often due to pregnancy.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the menstrual cycle are CORRECT?
1. The LH surge is a rapid, sharp rise in LH at mid-cycle. 2. The LH surge causes rupture of the Graafian follicle. 3. Oestrogen is secreted mainly by the corpus luteum. 4. Progesterone maintains the endometrium in preparation for implantation.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — oestrogen is secreted mainly by the growing follicles, not the corpus luteum (which secretes progesterone).

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the menstrual cycle are CORRECT?
1. Menstruation occurs when the released ovum is fertilised. 2. The fimbriae of the infundibulum pick up the ovum after ovulation. 3. The menstrual cycle is a reproductive cycle unique to primates. 4. The corpus luteum's degeneration causes a rise in progesterone.
q.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong — menstruation occurs when the ovum is NOT fertilised. Statement 4 is wrong — degeneration of the corpus luteum causes a FALL in progesterone.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about the menstrual cycle are CORRECT?
1. The menstrual phase typically lasts about 3–5 days. 2. Follicles grow and mature into a Graafian follicle during the follicular phase. 3. The endometrium regenerates during the luteal phase, not the follicular phase. 4. A new menstrual cycle begins if fertilisation does not occur.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — the endometrium regenerates during the follicular (proliferative) phase, not the luteal phase.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about fertilisation and early embryonic development are CORRECT?
1. Insemination is the release of semen into the vagina during coitus. 2. Fertilisation normally occurs in the vagina. 3. Fertilisation is also known as syngamy. 4. Sperms must reach the ampullary–isthmic junction to fertilise the ovum.
q.e: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong — fertilisation normally occurs at the ampullary-isthmic junction of the oviduct, not the vagina.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about fertilisation and early embryonic development are CORRECT?
1. The zona pellucida changes on sperm contact to block polyspermy. 2. Only one sperm normally fertilises an ovum. 3. The acrosome enzymes activate only after the zygote is formed. 4. Sperm entry induces the secondary oocyte to complete meiosis-II.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — the acrosome enzymes act BEFORE and DURING fertilisation, helping the sperm penetrate the ovum's coverings; they act well before the zygote forms.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about fertilisation and early embryonic development are CORRECT?
1. The human female is XY. 2. All human ova carry only an X chromosome. 3. About 50% of human sperms carry a Y chromosome. 4. An X-bearing sperm fertilising the ovum produces a male child.
q.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong — the human female is XX. Statement 4 is wrong — an X-bearing sperm gives an XX zygote, a female child.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about fertilisation and early embryonic development are CORRECT?
1. Cleavage of the zygote begins in the isthmus. 2. The 8–16 celled embryo stage is called the morula. 3. The morula transforms into the blastocyst as it moves into the uterus. 4. The blastocyst's inner cell mass attaches to the endometrium.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong — it is the trophoblast, not the inner cell mass, that attaches to the endometrium; the inner cell mass forms the embryo proper.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about fertilisation and early embryonic development are CORRECT?
1. Implantation is the embedding of the blastocyst in the endometrium. 2. Implantation leads to pregnancy. 3. The father's sperm type, not the mother's ovum, determines the sex of the child. 4. A Y-bearing sperm fertilising the ovum results in a female child.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong — a Y-bearing sperm gives an XY zygote, which develops into a male child.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about fertilisation and early embryonic development are CORRECT?
1. The trophoblast differentiates into the embryo proper. 2. The zygote undergoes rapid mitotic divisions called cleavage. 3. Blastomeres are the daughter cells formed by cleavage. 4. The secondary oocyte completes meiosis-I only after fertilisation.
q.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong — the inner cell mass, not the trophoblast, forms the embryo proper. Statement 4 is wrong — meiosis-I is completed earlier at the tertiary follicle stage; it is meiosis-II that completes after fertilisation.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about pregnancy, parturition and lactation are CORRECT?
1. The placenta forms after implantation, once chorionic villi appear on the trophoblast. 2. The placenta acts only as a nutrient-transport structure and produces no hormones. 3. The umbilical cord connects the embryo to the placenta. 4. hCG is one of the hormones produced only during pregnancy.
q.e: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong — the placenta also acts as an endocrine tissue, producing hormones like hCG and hPL.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about pregnancy, parturition and lactation are CORRECT?
1. Gastrulation forms the three primary germ layers: ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm. 2. The foetal heart is first detectable by the end of the first month. 3. By the end of the second month, the foetus develops limbs and digits. 4. By the end of 12 weeks, external genitalia are not yet formed at all.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong — by the end of 12 weeks (first trimester), external genitalia are well developed.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about pregnancy, parturition and lactation are CORRECT?
1. By the end of 24 weeks, the body is covered with fine hair and eyelids separate. 2. The average human gestation period is about 9 months (~40 weeks). 3. The foetal ejection reflex triggers release of prolactin, not oxytocin. 4. Oxytocin causes stronger uterine contractions in a positive feedback loop.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — the foetal ejection reflex triggers release of oxytocin, not prolactin.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about pregnancy, parturition and lactation are CORRECT?
1. After delivery of the baby, the placenta is also expelled. 2. Prolactin controls milk ejection, while oxytocin controls milk secretion. 3. Colostrum is rich in antibodies, especially IgA. 4. Breastfeeding in the initial period helps the infant develop immunity.
q.e: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong — it is reversed: prolactin controls milk SECRETION, and oxytocin controls milk EJECTION.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about pregnancy, parturition and lactation are CORRECT?
1. Relaxin is secreted mainly in the later phase of pregnancy. 2. Cortisol, prolactin and thyroxine levels also rise several-fold during pregnancy. 3. The corpus luteum, not the placenta, is the main hormone source late in pregnancy. 4. Human placental lactogen (hPL) is produced only during pregnancy.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — the placenta, not the corpus luteum, becomes the major hormone-producing tissue later in pregnancy.

q.q:
How many of the following statements about pregnancy, parturition and lactation are CORRECT?
1. The inner cell mass contains stem cells with the potency to form all tissues. 2. Parturition is triggered by a complex neuroendocrine mechanism. 3. The foetal ejection reflex is triggered by signals from the fully developed foetus and placenta. 4. A functional mammary gland develops for the first time only during a woman's second pregnancy.
q.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong — the mammary glands differentiate and become active during (and after) pregnancy generally, not specifically only during a second pregnancy.

q.q: If each of a testis's 250 lobules has the maximum stated number of seminiferous tubules (3), while another testis's lobules each have the minimum (1), what is the difference in total tubule count between the two testes?
q.e: Maximum total = 250 × 3 = 750 tubules. Minimum total = 250 × 1 = 250 tubules. Difference = 750 − 250 = 500.

q.q: Body core temperature is about 37°C. Given that the testes must be kept about 2–2.5°C cooler than this for normal spermatogenesis, what is the approximate scrotal temperature?
q.e: 37°C minus 2–2.5°C gives an approximate scrotal temperature of 34.5–35°C.

q.q: If each ovary is about 3 cm long (the midpoint of the 2–4 cm range) and a woman's oviduct is roughly 3.5 times as long as her ovary, approximately how long is one oviduct?
q.e: 3 cm × 3.5 = 10.5 cm, which falls within the stated 10–12 cm oviduct length range.

q.q: If a woman's left breast has 16 mammary lobes and her right breast has 19 (both within the normal 15–20 range), what is the total number of mammary lobes across both breasts?
q.e: 16 + 19 = 35 mammary lobes in total.

q.q: If 40 primary oocytes complete oogenesis normally, how many functional ova are produced in total (given that oogenesis yields only one functional gamete per mother cell)?
q.e: Unlike spermatogenesis, oogenesis produces only one functional ovum per primary oocyte (plus non-functional polar bodies), so 40 primary oocytes give 40 functional ova.

q.q: One primary spermatocyte yields 4 spermatids, while one primary oocyte yields only 1 functional ovum. How many more functional gametes does spermatogenesis produce per mother cell compared to oogenesis?
q.e: 4 (from spermatogenesis) − 1 (from oogenesis) = 3 more functional gametes per mother cell.

q.q: If a woman's cycle is 28 days long and the combined menstrual and follicular phases span the first 13 days, approximately what fraction of the cycle do these phases together represent?
q.e: 13/28 ≈ 0.46, i.e. about 46% of the cycle.

q.q: If ovulation occurs on day 14 of a 28-day cycle and the luteal phase runs from day 15 to day 28, how many days does the luteal phase last?
q.e: From day 15 to day 28 inclusive is 28 − 15 + 1 = 14 days.

q.q: Cleavage of the zygote produces 2, 4, 8, then 16 blastomeres over successive mitotic divisions. How many such divisions have occurred by the time the 16-cell stage is reached?
q.e: 2¹=2, 2²=4, 2³=8, 2⁴=16, so four successive mitotic divisions produce the 16-cell stage.

q.q: In a sample of 1,000 mature human ova, since all human ova carry only an X chromosome, how many would be expected to carry a Y chromosome?
q.e: Since the human female is XX, all ova carry only an X chromosome; none carry a Y chromosome.

q.q: If gestation lasts about 40 weeks and the second trimester ends at 24 weeks, approximately what fraction of the full gestation period has elapsed by the end of the second trimester?
q.e: 24/40 = 0.6, i.e. about 60% of the full gestation period.

q.q: If limb and digit development is seen by the end of month 2 (about 8 weeks) and major organ systems are formed by the end of week 12, approximately how many weeks pass between these two milestones?
q.e: 12 weeks − 8 weeks (end of month 2) = about 4 weeks between the two milestones.

q.q: Which sequence correctly represents the hormonal cascade regulating spermatogenesis at puberty?
o: Hypothalamus → Anterior pituitary → Leydig/Sertoli cells → Spermatogenesis
Anterior pituitary → Hypothalamus → Leydig/Sertoli cells → Spermatogenesis
Leydig/Sertoli cells → Hypothalamus → Anterior pituitary → Spermatogenesis
Hypothalamus → Leydig/Sertoli cells → Anterior pituitary → Spermatogenesis
q.e: The hypothalamus secretes GnRH, which acts on the anterior pituitary to release LH and FSH; these then act on Leydig and Sertoli cells respectively to drive spermatogenesis.

q.q: Which sequence correctly represents the parts of the oviduct from the ovary end to the uterine end?
q.e: From the ovary end to the uterine end, the oviduct runs: infundibulum (bears fimbriae) → ampulla (widest, usual fertilisation site) → isthmus (narrow, joins the uterus).

q.q: Which sequence correctly represents the process of spermatogenesis from spermatogonia to spermatozoa?
o: Spermatogonia → Secondary spermatocyte → Primary spermatocyte → Spermatid → Spermatozoon
Primary spermatocyte → Spermatogonia → Secondary spermatocyte → Spermatid → Spermatozoon
Spermatogonia → Primary spermatocyte → Spermatid → Secondary spermatocyte → Spermatozoon
Spermatogonia → Primary spermatocyte → Secondary spermatocyte → Spermatid → Spermatozoon
q.e: Spermatogonia (mitosis) → primary spermatocytes (meiosis-I) → secondary spermatocytes (meiosis-II) → spermatids → spermatozoa (via spermiogenesis).

q.q: Which sequence correctly represents the phases of the menstrual cycle in a 28–29 day cycle?
o: Menstrual phase → Follicular phase → Ovulatory phase → Luteal phase
Follicular phase → Menstrual phase → Ovulatory phase → Luteal phase
Menstrual phase → Ovulatory phase → Follicular phase → Luteal phase
Luteal phase → Menstrual phase → Follicular phase → Ovulatory phase
q.e: The cycle proceeds: menstrual phase (Days 1-5) → follicular phase (Days 5-13) → ovulatory phase (around Day 14) → luteal phase (Days 15-28).

q.q: Which sequence correctly represents the sex-determination pathway resulting in a male child?
o: X-bearing sperm produced by meiosis → fuses with X-bearing ovum → XY zygote formed → develops into male
Y-bearing sperm produced by meiosis → fuses with X-bearing ovum → XY zygote formed → develops into male
Y-bearing sperm produced by meiosis → fuses with Y-bearing ovum → XY zygote formed → develops into male
XY zygote formed → Y-bearing sperm produced → fuses with X-bearing ovum → develops into male
q.e: A Y-bearing sperm (formed by meiosis in the male) fuses with an X-bearing ovum (all ova carry X) to form an XY zygote, which develops into a male.

q.q: Which sequence correctly represents these gestational milestones in chronological order?
o: Limb and digit development (end of month 2) → Heart formation (end of month 1) → Major organ systems formed (end of 12 weeks) → Fine body hair and eyelid separation (end of 24 weeks)
Major organ systems formed (end of 12 weeks) → Heart formation (end of month 1) → Limb and digit development (end of month 2) → Fine body hair and eyelid separation (end of 24 weeks)
Heart formation (end of month 1) → Limb and digit development (end of month 2) → Major organ systems formed (end of 12 weeks) → Fine body hair and eyelid separation (end of 24 weeks)
Fine body hair and eyelid separation (end of 24 weeks) → Major organ systems formed (end of 12 weeks) → Limb and digit development (end of month 2) → Heart formation (end of month 1)
q.e: In chronological order: the heart forms by the end of month 1 → limbs and digits develop by the end of month 2 → major organ systems and external genitalia are well formed by the end of 12 weeks → fine body hair appears and eyelids separate by the end of 24 weeks.

q.q: Which of the following statements about the male reproductive system is INCORRECT?
o: The bulbourethral glands are a pair of larger glands than the prostate.
The testes lie inside the scrotum, outside the abdominal cavity.
GnRH from the hypothalamus stimulates the anterior pituitary to release LH and FSH.
Leydig cells secrete androgens under LH (ICSH) stimulation.
q.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — the bulbourethral glands are small, much smaller than the (single) prostate gland. The others are correct.

q.q: Which of the following statements about the female reproductive system is CORRECT?
o: The myometrium is the innermost uterine layer.
The ampulla is the widest part of the oviduct and the usual site of fertilisation.
The hymen reliably indicates whether a woman is sexually active.
The clitoris is a paired erectile gland.
q.e: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong (the endometrium is innermost). Statement 3 is wrong (the hymen is not a reliable indicator). Statement 4 is wrong (the clitoris is a single erectile structure, not a paired gland).

q.q: Which of the following statements about gametogenesis is INCORRECT?
o: Oogonia are formed only during foetal life.
GnRH acts directly on Leydig cells to release androgens.
The first meiotic division of the primary oocyte is unequal.
q.e: Statement 3 is incorrect — GnRH acts on the anterior pituitary, which releases LH; LH then acts on Leydig cells. The others are correct.

q.q: Among the following, identify the statement about the menstrual cycle that is CORRECT.
o: Progesterone is secreted mainly by the growing ovarian follicles.
Menstruation occurs when the ovum has been fertilised.
The luteal phase precedes the follicular phase.
q.e: Statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong (progesterone comes mainly from the corpus luteum). Statement 2 is wrong (menstruation occurs when NOT fertilised). Statement 3 is wrong (the follicular phase comes first).

q.q: Which of the following statements about fertilisation and early development is INCORRECT?
o: The inner cell mass of the blastocyst attaches to the uterine endometrium.
Fertilisation normally occurs at the ampullary–isthmic junction.
An XY zygote develops into a male child.
Cleavage of the zygote produces blastomeres.
q.e: Statement 1 is incorrect — it is the trophoblast, not the inner cell mass, that attaches to the endometrium. The others are correct.

q.q: Which of the following statements about pregnancy and lactation is CORRECT?
o: Oxytocin controls milk secretion, while prolactin controls milk ejection.
Colostrum, secreted during the initial days of lactation, is rich in antibodies such as IgA.
The corpus luteum, not the placenta, becomes the main hormone source late in pregnancy.
Relaxin is secreted throughout pregnancy at a constant level.
q.e: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong (it is reversed: prolactin controls secretion, oxytocin controls ejection). Statement 3 is wrong (the placenta becomes the major hormone source). Statement 4 is wrong (relaxin is secreted mainly in the later phase of pregnancy).

q.q: India was among the first countries in the world to initiate national action plans towards a reproductively healthy society. These programmes are currently known as:
o: Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes
q.e: The family planning programmes started in 1951 were periodically assessed and broadened in scope, and are today run as Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes.

q.q: Amniocentesis is legally banned in India when used for one particular purpose. Identify the purpose and the reason.
o: Detection of Down’s syndrome, because the test is unreliable
Detection of chromosomal abnormalities, because it harms the foetus
Assessment of foetal age, because it delays MTP
Determination of foetal sex, because it leads to female foeticide
q.e: Amniocentesis continues to be used for detecting genetic disorders and chromosomal abnormalities. Its misuse for sex determination, followed by abortion of female foetuses, led to the statutory ban on this specific use.

q.q: Which of the following combinations correctly describes ‘Saheli’?
o: Non-steroidal preparation, once-a-week pill, developed at CDRI Lucknow
Steroidal preparation, daily pill, developed at ICMR New Delhi
Non-steroidal preparation, daily pill, developed at CDRI Lucknow
Steroidal preparation, once-a-week pill, developed at CDRI Lucknow
q.e: Saheli is a new oral contraceptive for females developed by CDRI, Lucknow. It contains a non-steroidal preparation, is a once-a-week pill, has very few side effects and high contraceptive value.

q.q: The main reason for the population explosion in India is:
o: A sudden increase in the number of children born to each couple
Immigration of people from neighbouring countries
A rapid decline in death rate, MMR and IMR along with more people of reproducible age
Increase in the average human life span alone
q.e: Better health facilities and living conditions caused a rapid decline in the death rate, including maternal and infant mortality rates, while the number of people in the reproducible age group increased — together producing population explosion.

q.q: India’s population, which was about 350 million at the time of independence, crossed 1 billion by:
q.e: India’s population was roughly 350 million in 1947 and crossed the 1 billion mark by May 2000, making every sixth person in the world an Indian.

q.q: A contraceptive is said to be ideal if it is user-friendly, easily available, effective, free of major side effects and:
o: Capable of reducing the libido of the user
Reversible, without interfering with the user’s libido
q.e: An ideal contraceptive must be reversible so that fertility returns when its use is discontinued, and it must not interfere with the sexual drive, desire or sexual act of the user.

q.q: A couple practising the rhythm method avoids coitus from day 10 to day 17 of the cycle. The scientific basis of this is that:
o: Ovulation is expected during this period, so chances of fertilisation are highest
The endometrium is completely shed during this period
Cervical mucus becomes impenetrable during this period
q.e: Days 10 to 17 constitute the fertile period of a normal 28-day cycle because ovulation is expected around mid-cycle. Avoiding coitus then prevents the ovum and sperm from meeting.

q.q: Which of the following statements about condoms is INCORRECT?
o: They are made of thin rubber or latex sheath
They are available for both males and females
They are reusable barriers that cover the cervix
They protect the user against STDs and AIDS
q.e: Condoms are disposable and cover the penis in males or the vagina and cervix in females. The reusable barriers that cover the cervix are diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults.

q.q: Lactational amenorrhea is an effective natural contraceptive method because:
o: Breast milk contains a natural spermicide
The uterus remains contracted after delivery for one full year
The cervix stays closed throughout the lactation period
Ovulation and menstruation do not occur during intense lactation, but only up to 6 months after parturition
q.e: During the phase of intense lactation the mother does not menstruate or ovulate, so the chance of conception is almost nil. This protection is reliable only up to a maximum of six months after parturition.

q.q: Progestasert and LNG-20 are IUDs which act by:
o: Making the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms
Releasing Cu ions that suppress sperm motility
Causing a sterile inflammatory response only
q.e: Progestasert and LNG-20 are hormone-releasing IUDs. Besides the phagocytosis of sperms common to all IUDs, they make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.

q.q: Depo Provera, Implanon and Norplant are all:
q.e: Depo Provera is an injectable contraceptive, while Implanon and Levonorgestrel Norplant are implants placed under the skin. Their mode of action is similar to that of the pills but they are effective for much longer periods.

q.q: A woman is advised a contraceptive that will let her space her children and is one of the most widely accepted methods in India, acting mainly by increasing the phagocytosis of sperms in the uterus. The method is:
q.e: IUDs are inserted into the uterus by doctors or expert nurses, increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus, are ideal for delaying pregnancy or spacing children, and are among the most widely accepted contraceptives in India.

q.q: Tubectomy, a surgical contraceptive method in females, involves:
o: Removal/tying of a part of the fallopian tube
q.e: Tubectomy blocks ova transport by removing or tying off a part of the fallopian tube.

q.q: MTP is especially recommended to be performed within:
o: Any time, since risk is the same throughout
Only after the 20th week of pregnancy
The first trimester (up to 12 weeks), which is relatively safer
q.e: MTPs are relatively safe during the first trimester (up to 12 weeks); second-trimester abortions are much riskier.

q.q: The statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination was implemented mainly to prevent:
q.e: Amniocentesis was banned for sex determination to prevent its misuse in aborting female foetuses (female foeticide).

q.q: Which of the following STDs is known to spread also via blood transfusion, apart from sexual contact?
q.e: Hepatitis-B (like HIV) can spread through blood transfusion, infected needles, and mother-to-foetus transmission, besides sexual contact.

q.q: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) is best described as a:
o: Late complication of an untreated STD
q.e: PID is a late/untreated complication of STDs that can lead to infertility.

q.q: STDs show the highest reported incidence in which age group?
q.e: The 15–24 years age group reports the highest incidence of STDs.

q.q: Which of these is a male cause of infertility?
q.e: Cryptorchidism (absence of testes from the scrotum) is a male cause of infertility.

q.q: Normal human sperm count is generally considered to be in the range of:
q.e: Normal sperm count is 50–150 million/ml; a count below 20 million/ml is termed oligospermia.

q.q: Infertility is clinically defined as failure to conceive despite regular unprotected intercourse for about:
q.e: Infertility is commonly defined as failure to conceive after about 2 years of regular unprotected intercourse.

q.q: In IUT (Intra Uterine Transfer), the embryo transferred to the uterus is at a stage of:
q.e: In IUT, embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred directly into the uterus.
